title: [finding] create-objectstack's runtime-image test hard-codes minor 4, so it goes red on any minor bump — it blocks the 17.5.0 Version Packages PR (Test Core 1/6)
body:
## What happens

`packages/create-objectstack/src/runtime-image.test.ts:98` builds the CLI version the scaffold is expected to resolve as a literal minor:

```ts
const resolved = `${String(ownVersion).split('.')[0]}.4.2`;
```

The scaffolded `package.json` asks for `^<own version>`. While the train sits at 17.4.x, `17.4.2` satisfies `^17.4.0` and the test passes. Once `pnpm run version` moves the train to 17.5.0, the same test asserts:

> scaffolded Dockerfile pins :17.4.2 but the scaffolded package.json asks for "^17.5.0"

## Evidence

- Observed on the Version Packages PR #17076, head `c3e7fddc`, required check `Test Core (1/6)`.
- On `main` the literal is still there (line 98), and `packages/create-objectstack/package.json` is at `17.4.0`. So `main` is green only because the bump has not happened yet.
- Repro on `main`: set `packages/create-objectstack/package.json` `version` to `17.5.0` (what `pnpm run version` does), then run `pnpm --filter create-objectstack test`. The test goes red.

## Fix

Derive `resolved` from the package's own version so that it always satisfies the caret floor (same major, a minor above the floor). Then the test no longer depends on where the train is. The fix has to land on `main`. `changeset-release/main` is regenerated from `main` by the `version-pr` lane (`git reset --hard`), so a commit made there would be overwritten.

The class-level gap (a version-sensitive regression is only exercised after `pnpm run version`) is filed separately.
